study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Floris et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: A multimodal neural signature of face processing in autism within the fusiform gyrus

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: EU-AIMS/AIMS-2-TRIALS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) cohort. Data collected across six sites: King's College London (KCL), University of Cambridge (UCAM), Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre (RUNMC), University Medical Centre Utrecht (UMCU), Central Institute of Mental Health Mannheim (CIMH), and University Campus Bio-Medico Rome (UCBM).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Participants were part of the EU-AIMS/AIMS-2-TRIALS LEAP cohort. They underwent comprehensive clinical, cognitive and MRI assessment at one of six collaborating sites."

answer.LEAP: normative model training/testing (10-fold cross-validation across entire sample including both autistic and non-autistic individuals) and clinical/cognitive association analysis in autistic individuals

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The normative models were derived in an unbiased manner across the entire sample (N=204) under 10-fold cross-validation using Bayesian Linear Regression. Both autistic (N=99) and non-autistic individuals (N=105) were included in normative model estimation. The resulting Z-deviation maps were used for multimodal fusion (LICA) and subsequent group comparisons and clinical-cognitive association analyses.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Normative models were derived in an unbiased manner across the entire sample under tenfold cross-validation." "The final sample has both complete imaging data across four different imaging modalities and phenotypic information available consisting of 99 autistic (71 males, 28 females) and 105 NAI (71 males, 34 females) between 7 and 30 years"
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Floris2024.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modeling, L193-194; Methods / Sample characterization, L176

model-1.model-name: multimodal normative model (structure, rs-fMRI, task-fMRI, EEG)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The normative model was trained across the entire sample of 204 individuals (99 autistic + 105 non-autistic) using 10-fold cross-validation. Both autistic and non-autistic individuals were included together in the normative model training process. The model was trained separately for each of four imaging modalities (structure, rs-fMRI, task-fMRI, EEG) within the right and left fusiform gyrus ROIs.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "normative models were trained using Bayesian linear regression for each brain imaging modality within the right and left FFG region of interest (ROI) independently using age, sex and scanning site as covariates... Normative models were derived in an unbiased manner across the entire sample under tenfold cross-validation."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Overall sample age statistics derived from Table 1: Autistic (N=99): mean=18.62, sd=5.32, range=7.58-30.0; NAI (N=105): mean=18.3, sd=4.87, range=10.37-30.9. Weighted mean = (99*18.62 + 105*18.3)/204 = 18.46. Pooled SD = sqrt(((99-1)*5.32^2 + (105-1)*4.87^2)/(204-2)) = 5.10. Min age overall = 7.58 (from autism group), Max age overall = 30.9 (from NAI group). Train-phase specific values not reported due to 10-fold cross-validation approach.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Age: Autistic Mean 18.62, S.d. 5.32, Range 7.58-30.0; NAI Mean 18.3, S.d. 4.87, Range 10.37-30.9"

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Overall sample sex distribution from Table 1: Autistic (N=99): 71 males, 28 females; NAI (N=105): 71 males, 34 females. Total: 142 males (69.6%), 62 females (30.4%). Groups did not differ significantly in sex ratio (χ2=0.23, P=0.63). Train-phase specific values not reported due to 10-fold cross-validation approach.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Sex: Individuals with autism 71 M, 28 F; NAI 71 M, 34 F; χ2 = 0.23, P = 0.63"
